_README: RM MODULE BUILDINGS TEMPLATE
This file defines the WORKSHOPS and FURNACES your module injects,
graphics included, with no raws.
HOW TO USE THIS FILE:
1. Copy it into your mod's data/ folder.
2. Rename it to <yourmod>_buildings.json.
3. Change the module block below to your own prefix.
4. Replace the buildings array with your own content.
5. Put its PNG sheets in data/images/.
6. Hand it to RM from your listener as buildings_json, the way
rm-module-template-advanced.lua hands over its files.
THE UNDERSCORE CONVENTION:
Any key starting with an underscore is documentation. RM's engine
reads only the keys it knows about, so _README and _comment are
ignored at load time. Keep them, edit them, or delete them.
PREFIXING:
You write key. Key KILNETTE under prefix MYMOD_ becomes the
building MYMOD_KILNETTE.
PUTTING REACTIONS IN IT:
A reaction's building must be an entry in BUILDING_TYPES, in
refinish-module-types.lua. For a building of your own, add one:
type { 13 }, subtype { 23 } for a workshop, or type { 5 },
subtype { 7 } for a furnace, with custom = { -1 } and custom_code
set to the building's full ID (guide section 5.2).
PERMISSIONS:
None to write. RM permits every building carrying your prefix to
every civilization, so it shows in the build menu.
VALIDATION:
RM's validator does not check this file. The building injector
guards each building and logs what it could not do. Run preflight,
which does check it.
FULL FIELD DOCUMENTATION:
RM_MODULE_ENGINE_README.md, section 7.3.

module._comment: Identity block. Keep it the same as your other files. Its prefix becomes the module's prefix only when the module ships no materials, reactions or tools file.
module.name: RM Module Template

buildings._comment: REFERENCE ENTRY. Every field the schema accepts, with its default noted. Copy it, then delete the lines you do not need.
buildings._comment_key: Required. Uppercase, no spaces. The building's code is prefix + key.
buildings._comment_name: Default: the key. Preflight requires it.
buildings.name: Reference kiln
buildings._comment_class: WORKSHOP or FURNACE. In game it defaults to WORKSHOP; preflight requires it written.
buildings._comment_dim: Default [3, 3]. Width and height in tiles.
buildings._comment_workloc: Default: the centre, [floor(width / 2), floor(height / 2)]. The tile the worker stands on, counted from 0. Preflight checks it lies inside dim.
buildings._comment_block: Optional. One row per tile of height, top to bottom, each with one entry per tile of width: 1 blocks the tile, 0 leaves it open. Preflight checks the shape against dim.
buildings._comment_build_key: Default 0, no key. The key that picks it in the build menu: a df.interface_key name such as CUSTOM_SHIFT_K, or a number. An unknown name is logged.
buildings._comment_needs_magma: Default false. True for a building that needs magma.
buildings._comment_labors: build_labors: the labors that may build it, default ["MASON"]. labor_description: optional text naming them.
buildings._comment_tooltip: Optional. Lines of text, one string each.
buildings._comment_name_color: Default [0, 7, 1]. The colour triple [foreground, background, brightness] DF keeps for the building's name.
buildings._comment_build_items: What it is built from. Preflight requires at least one. Each item takes: type, a df.item_type name (NONE takes any item, narrowed by flags); subtype, a tool ID or a number, for a TOOL item; mat, a material token such as INORGANIC:IRON (one that does not resolve stops this building injecting, and the log says why); quantity, default 1; reaction_class; and flags1, flags2 and flags3, DF's job item flags by name, each true or false.
buildings._comment_graphics: Optional. image is the PNG, its path relative to your data folder; tile_dim is its tile size in pixels, default 32. The sheet holds the building in blocks of width x (height + 1) tiles. The first four blocks, left to right, are build stages 3, 2, 1 and 0. With overlay on (the default), four more blocks follow for the overlay layer. Default sheet size: 8 x width columns by height + 1 rows; set sheet_dim [columns, rows] when yours is laid out bigger, and origin [column, row] to start somewhere other than the top-left tile. A sheet whose tile count does not match is not used: the building injects without graphics, and the log gives both counts. The build menu icon is list_icon [column, row] on the same sheet, or icon_image, a separate PNG (icon_dim, its tile size, defaults to tile_dim); icon_image wins when both are set.

buildings._comment: EXAMPLE. A 3x3 workshop built from any building material, with its graphics and a separate icon.
buildings.name: Kilnette
